s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement of a digit with associated neurological symptoms and abnormal growth
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Tingling at the fingertip
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
Decreased sensation distally
Overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue on CT scan
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been enlarged since birth
The enlargement has progressed over time
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
There is limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
The overlying skin is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
Sensation is decreased distally
Laboratory studies are unremarkable
CT scan shows overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue
No abnormal vascular structures are present on CT scan

shortlist.label: Macrodystrophia lipomatosa
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's progressive enlargement of the left middle finger since birth, associated with tingling and limited flexion, matches the clinical presentation of macrodystrophia lipomatosa, a rare condition characterized by localized overgrowth of bone and soft tissue.

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: The CT scan showing overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue, without abnormal vascular structures, is consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a benign tumor that can cause progressive enlargement of a digit.

shortlist.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are also compatible with lipofibromatous hamartoma, a rare benign tumor that can cause localized overgrowth of soft tissue and bone.

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, neurofibroma is a possible diagnosis given the patient's neurological symptoms, such as tingling and decreased sensation, which can be associated with this condition.

shortlist.label: Isolated neural lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: This diagnosis is considered due to the patient's neurological symptoms and the presence of a lipomatous process on CT scan, although it is a rare condition and other diagnoses are more likely.

raw.rationale: The condition presents with progressive enlargement of the finger since birth, tenderness, and decreased sensation, which is consistent with macrodystrophia lipomatosa. The CT scan showing overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue without abnormal vascular structures also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: While it involves fatty tissue overgrowth, the specific presentation and CT findings are more characteristic of macrodystrophia lipomatosa.

rejected.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Considered but excluded due to specific CT findings and clinical presentation that better fit macrodystrophia lipomatosa.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple neurofibromas and other systemic features, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Isolated neural lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Excluded due to the lack of specific neural involvement and the characteristic CT findings of macrodystrophia lipomatosa.
